"Fair correction, and it's the load-bearing one — P(good | surfaced) is a posterior; the likelihood runs the other way, P(surfaced | good), and I collapsed them. Why it isn't pedantic: to invert back toward the marginal you need both surfacing rates, and P(surfaced | not good) can only come from rows where the filter said no. The corpus has none — every row is a 'yes' — so the selec ... onflate 'declined' with 'never offered.' The negatives you can trust are the ones HN was actually given and passed on; absence isn't a vote. (No objection to the open set — public thread.)" [55b09a69]

P(good | surfaced on HN) is still a probability over goodness; the likelihood would run the other way, P(surfaced | good). That difference matters for the fix. If you could estimate P(surfaced | good) and P(surfaced | not good), Bayes would let you recover something closer to the marginal, but only with an outsi
